page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.large is a storage-optimized server instance belonging to the i7ie family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance features 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 1250 GB NVMe SSD. The instance runs on the Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core Geekbench score is in the top tier (top 10%), and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show strong performance in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance is poor, with stress-ng multi-core scoring in the bottom 10% and Geekbench multi-core in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached read-only large block bandwidth scoring in the bottom 10% and cached small block read-only bandwidth in the bottom 25%.

The i7ie.large offers a high storage-to-compute ratio, providing 1250 GB of NVMe SSD storage alongside 16.0 GB of RAM on only 2 vCPUs. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring significant local storage capacity and high single-threaded performance without needing massive parallel processing. However, the low multi-core performance and weak memory bandwidth represent clear tradeoffs. This instance is best suited for lightweight database operations, local caching, single-threaded data processing, and storage-heavy workloads that do not demand high multi-threaded compute density.
